hero.headline: "Either you're with us or against us!" — and your child is choosing from options they don't want?
hero.subheadline: They don't want either option. But the third one has simply disappeared. This isn't a choice — it's a trap.

media.alt: A child facing an artificial choice between two options with no third path

pain.title: "Either-or" isn't a choice — it's a narrowed frame
pain.body:
"Either you're with us or against us", "either you do it or you're not a real friend". In a group, at school, in a chat. The child doesn't want either option — but the choice has already been imposed. They go along because they can't see a third way out.

This isn't a real choice — it's manipulation: options are deliberately narrowed to two so the child picks the "right" one. All other possibilities simply disappear. Without the skill to notice this, the child accepts the rules of someone else's game and chooses from what they've been given.

The result — decisions are made under pressure, even though there was always another way. The child feels cornered, when in reality there were more options all along.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
